title: Viva Engage: broadcast, meeting-based and custom events with moderated questions and anonymous posting
summary: The briefing correctly reports the legacy event creation deadline and the documented Teams controls, while distinguishing Engage-specific uncertainties. One minor qualification is needed: the Teams events PowerShell reference still labels the policy as preview.

claims.claim: The service description encourages transitioning to Engage events powered by Teams town hall.

claims.where: Scope; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The affected group is organisers who still use the legacy live event creation option in Microsoft Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Event organizers who still create events with the legacy live event option in Engage.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends telling legacy-option organisers about the change before December 7, 2026.
claims.quote: Tell organizers who use the legacy option about this change before December 7, 2026.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends pointing organisers to Engage events for new and upcoming events.
claims.quote: Point organizers to Engage events for new and upcoming events.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating documentation, training and guidance mentioning the legacy live event option.
claims.quote: Update any internal documentation, training materials or guidance that mentions the legacy live event option.

claims.claim: Teams event organisers and co-organisers can turn on Q&A moderation.
claims.quote: In Teams events, organizers and co-organizers can allow presenters to manage the Q&A sessions. They can also turn on moderation

claims.claim: Teams Q&A moderation permits reviewing and approving questions before they appear in the feed.
claims.quote: They can also turn on moderation to review and approve questions before they appear in the Q&A feed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: When a Teams meeting organiser enables anonymous Q&A posting, attendees' questions are ingested into the organiser's mailbox for eDiscovery.
claims.quote: If the meeting organizer enables anonymous posting, the questions attendees post are ingested into the organizer’s mailbox for eDiscovery.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not establish how Teams Q&A moderation or its meeting policy maps to the Engage event moderated feed.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "policy" "Q&A"; Viva Engage events enable disable admin moderated feed. Opened microsoftteams/manage-qna-for-teams and engage/organize-live-event; neither identifies the new Engage moderated feed as Teams Q&A.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The same organiser-mailbox handling and identity visibility for anonymous Engage event questions is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "anonymous" "mailbox"; Viva Engage events anonymous posting eDiscovery. Opened microsoftteams/manage-qna-for-teams and engage/organize-live-event; Teams anonymous Q&A is documented, but the Engage event mapping is not.

claims.claim: Engage calendar invitations can reach subscribed internal and external community members subject to preferences and organisational policies.
claims.quote: Invitations can be delivered to subscribed internal and external community members, subject to their preferences and applicable organizational policies.

claims.claim: Send calendar invitations is off by default.
claims.quote: Send calendar invitations is off by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The organiser manages calendar invitations separately for each event.
claims.quote: An event organizer must still turn on “Send calendar invitations” for the individual event.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 groups with more than 5,000 members, an administrator must update delivery restrictions in Microsoft Entra for invitation delivery.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 groups with more than 5,000 members, an administrator must update the group's delivery restrictions in Microsoft Entra to allow invitation delivery.

claims.claim: Both Teams events policy attendee settings default to Everyone, permitting any user to attend.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.claim: Learn does not establish that Teams event attendee policies govern events created in Engage.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage events broadcast meeting async licensing policies; "Engage events" "AllowTownhalls". Opened microsoftteams/set-up-events and engage/organize-live-event; attendee policy reach is described for Teams events, not the new Engage creation experience.

claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing for the new broadcast, meeting-based and custom Engage event capabilities is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "licens"; Viva Engage broadcast meeting custom events pricing meter charge license. Opened engage/setup, Viva Engage service description, microsoftteams/events-licensing and engage/organize-live-event; no new Engage event-specific entitlement was found.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage service description directs readers to Microsoft 365 plan comparisons for subscriptions enabling Viva Engage.
claims.quote: For detailed plan information on subscriptions that enable users for Microsoft Viva Engage, see the Microsoft 365 business plan comparison and Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan comparison.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage service description points to Product Terms for licensing terms.
claims.quote: For licensing terms and conditions for products and services purchased through Microsoft Commercial Volume Licensing Programs, see the Product Terms site.

claims.claim: Teams event capabilities and attendee capacity vary with the organiser's license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Teams events licensing overview does not explicitly state how its rules apply to events created in Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "licens"; Viva Engage broadcast meeting custom events pricing meter charge license. Opened microsoftteams/events-licensing in full; it describes Microsoft Teams events and does not mention Viva Engage creation or licensing.

claims.claim: No meter or charge specific to these new Engage event types is published in the sources examined.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage broadcast meeting custom events pricing meter charge license. Opened engage/setup, Viva Engage service description and microsoftteams/events-licensing; no separate meter or charge for the new Engage event types was found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The arrival default for the added Engage event capabilities is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "default" "moderation"; "Engage events" "default" "enabled". Read roadmap and supplied posts; opened engage/setup, engage/send-calendar-invites and Teams controls. Calendar defaults and legacy retirement do not state the new capabilities' arrival default.

claims.claim: Teams Q&A requires sign-ins for the Office 365 Viva Engage service to be enabled in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: To allow users in your organization to add Q&A to Teams meetings and events, you must confirm that sign-ins for the Office 365 Viva Engage service are enabled in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The Teams Q&A prerequisites page does not establish that the new Engage event feed shares that prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage events enable disable admin moderated feed anonymous posting eDiscovery prerequisites; "Engage events" "policy" "Q&A". Opened microsoftteams/manage-qna-for-teams and engage/setup; no mapping of the new Engage event feed to Teams Q&A prerequisites was found.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience reaches the scheduling control.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating large-audience Teams events.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled
claims.fix: Keep the command. Add to controls[0].note: 'The PowerShell reference still labels this policy as preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps, which states 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.'

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams events scheduling policy controls which users can create large-audience events such as town halls.
claims.quote: Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Turning the Teams event scheduling setting Off after an event is scheduled prevents the user from running or starting it.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Engagement > Q&A reaches the Q&A policy control.
claims.quote: Open the Teams admin center. Expand Meetings from the navigation pane. Under Meetings, select Meeting policies. Either select an existing policy or create a new one. Navigate to the Meeting Engagement section and toggle the Q&A setting On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -QnAEngagementMode Disabled prevents organisers with that policy from using Q&A in their meetings and events.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from using Q&A in meetings and events they create, use the following script: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -QnAEngagementMode Disabled

claims.where: controls[1].governs and scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Teams meeting policy determines which organisers can use Q&A in meetings and events.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control whether an organizer can use Q&A in their meetings and events.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn does not establish whether the large-audience Teams scheduling control governs the new Viva Engage event creation experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "AllowTownhalls"; Viva Engage events enable disable admin AllowTownhalls. Opened microsoftteams/set-up-events, Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference and engage/organize-live-event; no new Engage creation-policy mapping was found.

claims.claim: The Teams pages examined do not document separate admin settings for Q&A moderation and anonymous posting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "policy" "Q&A"; Viva Engage events moderated feed anonymous posting admin. Opened microsoftteams/manage-qna-for-teams and microsoftteams/set-up-events; they document a Q&A policy and organiser choices, not separate moderation or anonymous-posting admin settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes human organisers moderating and attendees posting, and describes no automated actions.
claims.quote: Organizers will have additional support for moderating the posted questions and conversations, and attendees can post questions anonymously.
